# neatHack Hackathon Summary

## Theme & Problem Statement
Build AI agents capable of operating autonomously on complex, multi-step tasks. The core challenge: "Build agents you'd trust to run without you watching." Projects must demonstrate agents handling substantial work from start to finish with minimal human intervention.

## What Teams Must Build
A single-track competition requiring AI agents (solo or multi-agent systems) that complete meaningful tasks independently. Example categories include fixing GitHub issues, researching questions with cited sources, monitoring systems for anomalies, coordinating multiple agents, and handling dynamic environments.

## Required Tools & Sponsors
Projects must integrate three mandatory platforms:
- **neatlogs**: Agent tracing and failure analysis
- **Entire**: Repository context and checkpoints for coding agents
- **cfo.ai**: Business planning (pricing, costs, revenue, runway)

Additional resources include LiteLLM (Claude/Nova models), AWS credits ($25 per team), and Crustdata APIs (5,000 credits).

## Timeline & Deadlines
- **October 10–12, 2026**: 48-hour build window
- **October 10, 12:30 PM IST**: Hackathon begins
- **October 12, 7:00–11:55 PM IST**: Submission window
- **October 16**: Winners announced

## Submission Requirements
Teams must provide: public GitHub repository with hackathon-dated commits, demo video, neatlogs traces, Entire checkpoints, cfo.ai business plan, and evidence of "building in public" via social sharing.

## Judging Criteria (Weighted)
- Agent capability: 30%
- Tool integration effectiveness: 25%
- Demo clarity: 20%
- Public sharing: 15%
- Usefulness/originality: 10%

## Prizes
- **1st**: $2,000 + $5,000 Dodo Payments credits + 3 months Pro
- **2nd**: $1,000 + $3,000 credits + 3 months Pro
- **3rd**: $500 + $1,000 credits + 3 months Pro
- **Community Winner**: $500 (separate award for impact)

**Total**: $19,000 in cash and credits

## Key Rules
Teams can participate solo or in groups. Pre-hackathon setup allowed (infrastructure, frameworks), but core agent logic must be built during the event. All code must be publicly committed with proper timestamps for verification.

**Three tools you must use (no exceptions):**

2. **Entire**: connect your GitHub repo, install the CLI and capture checkpoints while you build. Your submission needs a checkpoint link and ID.
3. **cfo.ai**: make a business plan for the agent (pricing, costs, revenue, runway). Cancel the subscription right after signing up so your card isn't charged.

Optional extras: 5,000 Crustdata credits (company and people data), $25 in AWS credits per team, and Claude/Nova models through LiteLLM.

**Timeline (IST):**
- It started Oct 10 at 12:30 PM, so you have about a day and a half left.
- **Submissions are open Oct 12, 7:00–11:55 PM.**
- Winners are announced Oct 16.

**What to submit:**
- A public GitHub repo with commits dated during the hackathon (the core agent logic has to be written during the event)
- A demo video
- neatlogs traces
- An Entire checkpoint
- The cfo.ai business plan
- Proof you shared your progress publicly, such as social media posts

**How it's judged:**

| Criterion | Weight |
|---|---|
| How well the agent works | 30% |
| How well you use the three tools | 25% |
| How clear the demo is | 20% |
| Sharing your progress publicly | 15% |
| Usefulness and originality | 10% |

**Prizes:** $2,000, $1,000 and $500 for 1st to 3rd place, plus credits. There's also a separate $500 Community award.

**My take:** 45% of the score comes from using the tools and posting publicly, not from the agent itself. So set up neatlogs and Entire first, before you write agent code, and post progress updates as you go. Pick a task the agent can complete reliably from start to finish, and make the demo show it running without help, with the neatlogs traces on screen.

Here are six ideas, ranked by how well I think each one fits the judging criteria and the time you have left (about 1.5 days).

### 1. Agent Doctor: an agent that fixes other agents ⭐ my top pick
You point it at a broken agent. It reads that agent's **neatlogs traces**, works out why it failed (a bad tool call, a hallucination, a loop, a prompt problem), patches the code or prompt, runs it again, and **checks the new traces to confirm the fix worked**. It saves an **Entire checkpoint** before and after each fix, and it opens a PR.
- **Why it wins:** neatlogs and Entire are the core of the product, not add-ons, which plays straight into the 25% tool-integration score. The sponsors will love it.
- **Demo:** start with a deliberately buggy agent showing red traces. Doctor runs with no help, and the traces turn green.
- **Business angle for cfo.ai:** "Self-healing for agent teams," priced per fix.

### 2. Signal Hunter: an autonomous sales agent that reads hiring data
It uses **Crustdata** to watch for companies whose hiring suddenly jumps in one area (for example, a company that just posted 6 data engineer jobs). It infers what problem they're about to have, finds the right decision-maker, and writes a personalized pitch that cites its evidence.
- **Why it's cool:** most sales bots spam everyone. This one only reaches out when there's a real buying signal.
- It uses all of the free credits and has a natural cfo.ai pricing story.

### 3. Shadow Analyst: an autonomous investment memo
Give it a startup name. It pulls the company and team history from Crustdata, follows headcount trends, finds red flags (executive departures, hiring freezes), and writes a **cited investment memo** with a bull case and a bear case.
- **Demo:** type in a well-known startup and get a full analyst report in about 3 minutes, with every claim linked to a source.

### 4. Crash Test Dummy: a red-team agent that attacks other agents
It generates adversarial inputs against a target agent (prompt injections, edge cases, contradictory instructions), logs every failure in neatlogs, groups the failures by type, and produces a "safety report card."
- This fits the theme ("agents you'd trust") very directly. It pairs well with idea 1 if you want two agents working together: one breaks, the other fixes.

### 5. Night Shift: an overnight maintenance agent for repos
Give it a repo. It upgrades dependencies, runs the tests, fixes whatever broke, and opens a clean PR with an Entire checkpoint trail you can review in the morning.
- It's practical and easy to demo. It's less original, but it's very solid.

### 6. Incident Commander
It watches a log stream from a simulated service. When it spots an anomaly, it investigates, finds the root cause, suggests or applies a fix, and writes the postmortem itself.
- It's dramatic to demo, but you'd need to build a fake system to break, which costs time.

---

**My recommendation:** go with **#1 (Agent Doctor)**, or combine **#4 and #1** into a "break it, then heal it" setup if your team has 3 or more people. It scores highest on tool integration, it's original, and the demo shows a clear before-and-after. If you'd rather do something with commercial appeal, **#2** is the strongest product pitch.

## Your setup checklist (about 30–40 min)

### 1. GitHub repo (5 min)
1. Create a **public** GitHub repo, for example `agent-doctor`. Leave it empty, with no README.
2. Link this folder to it:
   ```bash
   cd ~/Bhargav/Neathack
   git init
   git remote add origin https://github.com/<you>/agent-doctor.git
   ```
3. Add your teammates as collaborators.

### 2. neatlogs (10 min)
1. Sign up at https://app.neatlogs.com and create a workspace and a project.
2. Go to **Settings → API keys** and copy the **project API key**. The page shows two keys, so make sure you copy the project one.

### 3. Entire (10 min)
1. Every teammate signs in at https://entire.io using **Sign in with GitHub**.
2. Install the **Entire GitHub App** on the repo's account or organization. If the repo is under an organization, an admin has to do this.
3. Install the CLI. The guide only gives the macOS (`brew`) command, so get the Linux install from the Entire docs.
4. In this folder, run:
   ```bash
   entire enable --agent claude-code
   ```
   If `claude-code` isn't accepted as the agent name, run `entire enable --help` and choose the Claude option.

### 4. LLM access (5 min)
Get the **LiteLLM key and base URL** from the hackathon guide or Discord. That's the free Claude access, and it's what the agents will run on. If you can't get it, an Anthropic API key works too.

### 5. cfo.ai (5 min, can be done later)
Sign up at https://cfo.ai/neathacks, then go to **Settings → Billing and cancel the subscription right away** so your card isn't charged. We'll build the business plan near the end.

### 6. Put the keys in a `.env` file in this folder
```
NEATLOGS_API_KEY=...
LITELLM_API_KEY=...
LITELLM_BASE_URL=...
GITHUB_TOKEN=...        # a GitHub personal access token with repo scope, so Doctor can open PRs
```
Don't paste the keys into this chat. Just create the file and tell me when it's there. I'll add `.env` to `.gitignore` so the keys never get committed.

### 7. Share publicly (keep doing this throughout)
Public sharing is 15% of the score. Post a "Day 1: building Agent Doctor for #neatHack" update on X or LinkedIn now, and post again at each milestone. I'll remind you when there's something worth posting.

---

1. Set up the project structure (Python, wired to LiteLLM and neatlogs).
2. Build a **"patient" agent**: a small agent with bugs planted on purpose so it fails in ways that show up in the traces.
3. Build **Agent Doctor**, which runs in a loop: read the traces → diagnose the failure → patch the code → run the patient again → check the new traces → commit with an Entire checkpoint → open a PR.
4. Write a demo script and a README you can record the demo video from.
5. Write the inputs for the cfo.ai business plan.

**Deadline reminder:** submissions close **tomorrow (Oct 12) at 11:55 PM IST**. We want the build done by tomorrow afternoon, so there's time left to record the video.

"""Expense-auditor agent: converts a trip's receipts to USD, totals them, and flags policy violations."""
import json

import neatlogs

from agent_doctor.llm import PATIENT_MODEL, get_client
from patient.tools import TOOL_FUNCTIONS, TOOL_SCHEMAS

MAX_STEPS = 12

SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are an expense auditor. For the receipts you are given:
1. Convert every item to USD using get_exchange_rate (multiply the amount by the rate).
2. Use calculate for all arithmetic.
3. Run check_policy on every item.
4. When done, reply with ONLY a JSON object, no prose:
   {"total_usd": <number rounded to 2 decimals>, "violations": [<category of each item over its limit>]}"""


@neatlogs.span(kind="AGENT")
def audit_expenses(receipts: str) -> dict:
    client = get_client()
    messages = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT}, {"role": "user", "content": receipts}]

    for _ in range(MAX_STEPS):
        response = client.chat.completions.create(model=PATIENT_MODEL, messages=messages, tools=TOOL_SCHEMAS)
        msg = response.choices[0].message
        messages.append(msg.model_dump(exclude_none=True))

        if not msg.tool_calls:
            return parse_report(msg.content)

        for call in msg.tool_calls:
            args = json.loads(call.function.arguments)
            result = TOOL_FUNCTIONS[call.function.name](**args)
            messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call.id, "content": json.dumps(result)})

    raise RuntimeError(f"agent did not finish within {MAX_STEPS} steps")


def parse_report(text: str) -> dict:
    data = json.loads(text.strip().removeprefix("```json").removesuffix("```"))
    return {"total": float(data["total"]), "violations": sorted(data["violations"])}

"""Run the patient's test suite. Every case is one neatlogs trace, grouped by --session.

    python -m patient.run --session exam-123 --out results.json
"""
import argparse
import json
import traceback

import neatlogs

from patient.agent import audit_expenses
from patient.cases import CASES, grade


def run_case(case: dict, session: str) -> dict:
    with neatlogs.trace(f"expense-audit:{case['id']}", session_id=session, case_id=case["id"]):
        try:
            report = audit_expenses(case["receipts"])
            passed, reason = grade(report, case["expected"])
            return {"id": case["id"], "passed": passed, "reason": reason, "output": report}
        except Exception as e:
            return {
                "id": case["id"],
                "passed": False,
                "reason": f"crashed: {type(e).__name__}: {e}",
                "traceback": traceback.format_exc(limit=6),
            }


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--session", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--out")
    parser.add_argument("--case", help="run a single case id")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    cases = [c for c in CASES if not args.case or c["id"] == args.case]
    results = [run_case(c, args.session) for c in cases]
    neatlogs.flush()

    for r in results:
        print(f"{'PASS' if r['passed'] else 'FAIL'}  {r['id']:<18} {r['reason']}")
    print(f"{sum(r['passed'] for r in results)}/{len(results)} passed")
    if args.out:
        with open(args.out, "w") as f:
            json.dump(results, f, indent=2)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Agent Doctor: examines a failing agent through its neatlogs traces, patches it, and proves the fix."""
import json
import subprocess
import sys
import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

import neatlogs

from agent_doctor import ui
from agent_doctor.llm import DOCTOR_MODEL, ROOT, get_client
from agent_doctor.neatlogs_api import NeatlogsAPI

PATIENT_DIR = ROOT / "patient"
# Ground truth and the test harness are off limits: the Doctor fixes the agent, not the exam.
PROTECTED = {"patient/cases.py", "patient/run.py"}
MAX_TRACE_CHARS = 7000
MAX_TRACES_PER_ROUND = 3

DOCTOR_PROMPT = """You are Agent Doctor, an expert at debugging LLM agents from their execution traces.

You get: the agent's source code, its test results, and neatlogs traces of the failing runs
(every LLM call, tool call, arguments, outputs and exceptions).

Find the ROOT CAUSE of the failures. Ground every claim in the traces: quote the span, tool
arguments or error that proves it. Fix the agent's code, never the tests. Prefer the smallest
change that fixes the root cause. Failures can be layered: a crash may hide a logic bug that only
shows once the crash is fixed, so fix what the evidence supports and keep tool contracts consistent.

Reply with ONLY a JSON object:
{
  "diagnosis": "<one-line headline of the bug>",
  "root_cause": "<2-4 sentences explaining why the agent fails>",
  "evidence": ["<quote or fact from a trace>", ...],
  "edits": [{"file": "patient/<file>.py", "find": "<exact unique snippet>", "replace": "<new snippet>"}]
}
Each "find" must match the current file exactly once, including whitespace."""


@dataclass
class Exam:
    session: str
    results: list[dict]
    traces: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def passed(self) -> int:
        return sum(r["passed"] for r in self.results)

    @property
    def crashes(self) -> int:
        return sum(r["reason"].startswith("crashed") for r in self.results)

    @property
    def score(self) -> tuple[int, int]:
        return (self.passed, -self.crashes)

    def totals(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "tokens": sum(t.get("totalTokens") or 0 for t in self.traces),
            "cost": sum(t.get("totalCostUsd") or 0 for t in self.traces),
            "llm_calls": sum(t.get("llmCallsCount") or 0 for t in self.traces),
            "tool_calls": sum(t.get("toolCallsCount") or 0 for t in self.traces),
        }


class Doctor:
    def __init__(self, max_rounds: int = 4, open_pr: bool = True):
        self.client = get_client()
        self.api = NeatlogsAPI()
        self.max_rounds = max_rounds
        self.open_pr = open_pr
        self.stamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")
        self.branch = f"doctor/heal-{self.stamp}"
        self.run_dir = ROOT / ".doctor_runs" / self.stamp
        self.run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.history: list[dict] = []

    # ---- examination -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    @neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL")
    def examine(self, label: str) -> Exam:
        session = f"exam-{self.stamp}-{label}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:4]}"
        out = self.run_dir / f"{label}.json"
        ui.step(f"Examining patient  [dim](session {session})[/]")
        subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-m", "patient.run", "--session", session, "--out", str(out)],
            cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900,
        )
        exam = Exam(session, json.loads(out.read_text()))
        ui.step("Pulling traces from neatlogs")
        exam.traces = self.api.session_traces(session, expected=len(exam.results))
        ui.exam_table(exam)
        return exam

    def trace_evidence(self, exam: Exam) -> str:
        """Export the failing runs' traces from neatlogs as the Doctor's primary evidence."""
        by_case = {t.get("traceName", "").split(":", 1)[-1]: t for t in exam.traces}
        sections = []
        for r in [r for r in exam.results if not r["passed"]][:MAX_TRACES_PER_ROUND]:
            trace = by_case.get(r["id"])
            if not trace:
                sections.append(f"### case {r['id']}: no trace found in neatlogs")
                continue
            md = self.api.export_markdown(trace["traceId"])
            if len(md) > MAX_TRACE_CHARS:
                md = md[: MAX_TRACE_CHARS // 2] + "\n...[truncated]...\n" + md[-MAX_TRACE_CHARS // 2 :]
            sections.append(f"### case {r['id']} - trace {trace['traceId']} (status {trace.get('status')})\n{md}")
        return "\n\n".join(sections)

    # ---- diagnosis & treatment ---------------------------------------------------------------

    @neatlogs.span(kind="AGENT")
    def diagnose(self, exam: Exam) -> dict:
        ui.step(f"Diagnosing with {DOCTOR_MODEL}")
        sources = "\n\n".join(
            f"=== {p.relative_to(ROOT)} ===\n{p.read_text()}"
            for p in sorted(PATIENT_DIR.glob("*.py"))
            if str(p.relative_to(ROOT)) not in PROTECTED and p.name != "__init__.py"
        )
        results = json.dumps([{k: v for k, v in r.items() if k != "traceback"} for r in exam.results], indent=1)
        history = json.dumps(self.history, indent=1) if self.history else "none"
        user = (
            f"## Agent source\n{sources}\n\n## Test results\n{results}\n\n"
            f"## Previous treatment rounds\n{history}\n\n## neatlogs traces of failing runs\n{self.trace_evidence(exam)}"
        )
        response = self.client.chat.completions.create(
            model=DOCTOR_MODEL,
            messages=[{"role": "system", "content": DOCTOR_PROMPT}, {"role": "user", "content": user}],
            max_tokens=4000,
        )
        text = response.choices[0].message.content.strip()
        text = text[text.find("{") : text.rfind("}") + 1]
        plan = json.loads(text)
        ui.diagnosis(plan)
        return plan

    def apply(self, edits: list[dict]) -> list[str]:
        """Apply find/replace edits; everything is validated before any file is written."""
        pending: dict[Path, str] = {}
        for e in edits:
            if e["file"] in PROTECTED or not e["file"].startswith("patient/"):
                raise ValueError(f"refusing to edit {e['file']}")
            path = ROOT / e["file"]
            text = pending.get(path, path.read_text())
            if text.count(e["find"]) != 1:
                raise ValueError(f"'find' snippet matched {text.count(e['find'])} times in {e['file']}")
            pending[path] = text.replace(e["find"], e["replace"])
        for path, text in pending.items():
            path.write_text(text)
        ui.patch(edits)
        return [str(p.relative_to(ROOT)) for p in pending]

    def revert(self, files: list[str]):
        subprocess.run(["git", "checkout", "--", *files], cwd=ROOT, check=True)

    def commit(self, plan: dict, files: list[str], before: Exam, after: Exam):
        msg = (
            f"Doctor: {plan['diagnosis']}\n\n{plan['root_cause']}\n\n"
            f"Tests: {before.passed}/{len(before.results)} -> {after.passed}/{len(after.results)} passing\n"
            f"Evidence session: {before.session}\nVerified in session: {after.session}"
        )
        git(["add", *files])
        git(["commit", "-m", msg])

    # ---- main loop ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    @neatlogs.span(kind="WORKFLOW")
    def heal(self) -> dict:
        ui.banner()
        start_branch = git(["rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD"]).strip()
        if git(["status", "--porcelain", "patient"]).strip():
            raise RuntimeError("patient/ has uncommitted changes; commit or stash them first")
        git(["checkout", "-b", self.branch])

        first = current = self.examine("intake")
        round_no = 0
        while current.passed < len(current.results) and round_no < self.max_rounds:
            round_no += 1
            ui.round_header(round_no, self.max_rounds)
            try:
                plan = self.diagnose(current)
                files = self.apply(plan["edits"])
            except (ValueError, KeyError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
                ui.warn(f"Treatment plan unusable: {e}")
                self.history.append({"round": round_no, "error": str(e)})
                continue

            after = self.examine(f"round{round_no}")
            outcome = {
                "round": round_no, "diagnosis": plan["diagnosis"], "files": files,
                "before": f"{current.passed}/{len(current.results)}", "after": f"{after.passed}/{len(after.results)}",
                "after_failures": [r["reason"] for r in after.results if not r["passed"]],
            }
            if after.score > current.score:
                self.commit(plan, files, current, after)
                ui.ok(f"Improvement verified in traces: {outcome['before']} -> {outcome['after']}. Committed.")
                outcome["kept"] = True
                current = after
            else:
                self.revert(files)
                ui.warn(f"No improvement ({outcome['before']} -> {outcome['after']}). Patch reverted.")
                outcome["kept"] = False
            self.history.append(outcome)

        report = self.write_report(first, current)
        if any(h.get("kept") for h in self.history) and self.open_pr:
            self.publish(report, first, current)
        else:
            git(["checkout", start_branch])
        ui.summary(first, current)
        return {"before": first.passed, "after": current.passed, "branch": self.branch}

    # ---- reporting ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def write_report(self, first: Exam, last: Exam) -> Path:
        b, a = first.totals(), last.totals()
        lines = [
            f"# Agent Doctor report - {self.stamp}",
            "",
            f"**Result:** {first.passed}/{len(first.results)} -> **{last.passed}/{len(last.results)}** test cases passing",
            "",
            "| | Before | After |",
            "|---|---|---|",
            f"| Passing cases | {first.passed}/{len(first.results)} | {last.passed}/{len(last.results)} |",
            f"| Crashes | {first.crashes} | {last.crashes} |",
            f"| LLM calls | {b['llm_calls']} | {a['llm_calls']} |",
            f"| Tool calls | {b['tool_calls']} | {a['tool_calls']} |",
            f"| Tokens | {b['tokens']} | {a['tokens']} |",
            "",
            f"neatlogs sessions: before `{first.session}`, after `{last.session}`",
            "",
            "## Treatment log",
        ]
        for h in self.history:
            if "error" in h:
                lines.append(f"- Round {h['round']}: plan rejected ({h['error']})")
            else:
                verdict = "kept" if h["kept"] else "reverted"
                lines.append(f"- Round {h['round']}: **{h['diagnosis']}** ({h['before']} -> {h['after']}, {verdict})")
        path = ROOT / "reports" / f"heal-{self.stamp}.md"
        path.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
        git(["add", str(path.relative_to(ROOT))])
        git(["commit", "-m", f"Doctor: add healing report {self.stamp}"])
        return path

    def publish(self, report: Path, first: Exam, last: Exam):
        ui.step(f"Pushing {self.branch} and opening a pull request")
        git(["push", "-u", "origin", self.branch])
        title = f"Agent Doctor: patient healed ({first.passed}/{len(first.results)} -> {last.passed}/{len(last.results)})"
        body = report.read_text() + "\n\n🤖 Opened autonomously by Agent Doctor"
        pr = subprocess.run(
            ["gh", "pr", "create", "--head", self.branch, "--title", title, "--body", body],
            cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True,
        )
        ui.ok(f"Pull request: {pr.stdout.strip()}" if pr.returncode == 0 else f"PR failed: {pr.stderr.strip()}")


def git(args: list[str]) -> str:
    return subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=ROOT, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout

# Agent Doctor

**An AI agent that fixes other AI agents, and proves the fix through traces.**

Agents fail in ways unit tests don't catch: a tool schema drifts from its implementation, a prompt and a parser disagree on a key, a rate gets inverted. The evidence is in the execution traces, but someone has to read them. Agent Doctor reads them for you.

Point it at a failing agent and it runs on its own:

1. **Examine:** runs the agent's test suite. Every run is traced in [neatlogs](https://neatlogs.com).
2. **Read the traces:** pulls each failing run back through the neatlogs public API: every LLM call, tool call, argument, output and exception.
3. **Diagnose:** finds the root cause and quotes the spans that prove it.
4. **Treat:** patches the agent's code. It never touches the tests.
5. **Verify:** re-runs the suite. A patch is kept only if the new traces show the original failure gone and nothing regressed; otherwise it's reverted and the Doctor tries again with that lesson in hand.
6. **Discharge:** commits each verified fix (each commit carries an [Entire](https://entire.io) checkpoint), writes a before/after report, and opens a pull request.

## Demo: the patient

[`patient/`](patient/) is an expense-auditor agent: it converts receipts to USD, totals them, and flags travel-policy violations. It ships with three layered bugs, each hidden behind the previous one:

| Layer | Bug | Symptom in traces |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Tool schema says `meal/hotel/taxi`, policy table uses `meals/lodging/transport` | `check_policy` span → `KeyError: 'meal'` |
| 2 | Prompt asks for `total_usd`, parser reads `total` | final LLM output is correct, run still crashes |
| 3 | Exchange rates are inverted | `calculate("150 * 0.92")`: the totals are wrong |

A typical run:

```
0/4 passing, 4 crashed
Round 1  schema/policy key mismatch   → original failure cleared, deeper bug exposed
Round 2  parser reads wrong key       → 0/4 → 1/4
Round 3  inverted exchange rates      → 1/4 → 4/4
Discharge summary: 0/4 → 4/4 passing, crashes 4 → 0  (PR opened)
```

## Run it

```bash
python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env   # fill in keys
.venv/bin/python -m patient.run --session try-1     # see the patient fail
.venv/bin/python -m agent_doctor heal               # heal it and open a PR
.venv/bin/python -m agent_doctor heal --no-pr       # heal locally only
```

`.env`:

| Variable | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` | project key, used by the SDK to send traces |
| `NEATLOGS_PUBLIC_API_KEY` | service-account token (`nlsa_…`), used by the Doctor to read traces |
| `LITELLM_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_BASE_URL` | OpenAI-compatible endpoint (neatHack LiteLLM) |
| `GITHUB_TOKEN` | pushes the treatment branch |

The patient runs on `claude-haiku` and the Doctor on `claude-sonnet-4.6` (override with `PATIENT_MODEL` / `DOCTOR_MODEL`).

## How it uses the stack

- **neatlogs** is both the Doctor's eyes and its proof. The SDK traces the patient (and the Doctor's own reasoning). The public API (`/traces`, `/spans`, `/spans/{id}/payload`) gives the Doctor span-level inputs, outputs and errors to diagnose from. A re-run's traces are the evidence that a fix worked.
- **Entire** records every treatment commit as a checkpoint, so each fix is linked to the session context that produced it.
- **cfo.ai** was used to plan pricing, costs and runway for Agent Doctor as a product (see submission).

## Layout

```
agent_doctor/
  doctor.py         examine → diagnose → treat → verify loop, git + PR
  neatlogs_api.py   neatlogs public API client (traces, spans, payload timelines)
  llm.py            traced LiteLLM client
  ui.py             terminal presentation
patient/
  agent.py, tools.py   the agent under treatment
  cases.py, run.py     ground truth + harness (off limits to the Doctor)
reports/            healing reports written by the Doctor
```

# Agent Doctor: business plan inputs for cfo.ai

## Product, in one line
Self-healing for AI agents. Agent Doctor reads an agent's traces, finds the root cause of failures, patches the code, and opens a PR only when re-run traces prove the fix worked.

## Customer
- **Primary:** engineering teams running LLM agents in production (AI-native startups, 5–50 engineers) who already collect traces but have nobody with time to read them.
- **Secondary:** platform/ML teams at mid-size companies running 10+ internal agents.
- **Distribution:** an integration inside observability tools (neatlogs first), GitHub Marketplace app, open-source CLI as top of funnel.

## Pricing
The hook: **you pay for verified fixes, not attempts.** A heal that doesn't verify against the traces isn't counted.

| Plan | Price | Included | Who |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | 20 verified fixes/month, 1 agent, CLI only | individual devs, OSS |
| Pro | $99/month | 250 verified fixes, 5 agents, auto-PR | small teams |
| Team | $499/month | 2,000 verified fixes, unlimited agents, CI auto-heal on failing evals, Slack alerts | growing AI teams |
| Enterprise | from $2,500/month | self-hosted / bring-your-own-model, SSO, audit log | larger companies |

Overage: $0.50 per verified fix above the plan's allowance.

## Unit economics (measured during the hackathon)
- LLM cost per healing run: **≈ $0.18** (patient re-runs on Claude Haiku + 3 diagnosis rounds on Claude Sonnet). Measured: $0.79 total across ~5 full runs.
- Budget assumption: **$0.25 per run** to cover larger agents and retries.
- Hosting/infra: $300/month (workers, queue, DB) for the first year.
- Gross margin target: ~75% (Pro at full allowance = $62 LLM cost on $99; typical usage is ~40% of allowance).

## Costs (monthly)
| Item | Months 1–6 | Months 7–12 |
|---|---|---|
| Founders (3, India, stipends) | $4,500 | $7,500 |
| Infrastructure | $300 | $800 |
| LLM cost (COGS) | 25% of revenue | 25% of revenue |
| Tools & SaaS | $200 | $400 |
| Marketing (content, launches, events) | $500 | $2,000 |
| First hire (developer relations, from month 9) | – | $2,500 |

## Revenue assumptions (customers at end of month)
| Month | Pro | Team | Enterprise | MRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | $0 |
| 3 | 10 | 0 | 0 | $990 |
| 6 | 40 | 5 | 0 | $6,455 |
| 9 | 80 | 12 | 1 | $16,408 |
| 12 | 120 | 25 | 2 | $28,355 |

Churn: 4%/month on Pro, 2% on Team. Free→Pro conversion: 4%.

## Funding
- Starting cash: $25,000 (founders + hackathon prize money and credits)
- Planned pre-seed raise: $250,000 in month 6
- Goal: default-alive (MRR covers costs) by month 10–12.

## Questions for cfo.ai to answer
1. Runway with and without the month-6 raise.
2. Break-even month.
3. Sensitivity: what if LLM cost per run doubles, or Pro conversion is 2% instead of 4%?
